Modeling Earl’s plots as vertices of a graph, with edges between orthogonally adjacent green cells, gives a graph that is disconnected (at least one green plot has no adjacent green neighbor). A closed walk visiting every vertex exactly once (Hamiltonian cycle) requires the graph to be connected and every vertex to have degree ≥ 2. Because these conditions fail, such a walk is impossible.

The final rate equation given in the 1913 Michaelis–Menten paper is
v = (V · [S]) / (K_m + [S]).
Assuming V = k_cat (for a unit enzyme concentration), plug in Reaction 7 values:
[S] = 72.3, k_cat = 0.0429, K_m = 0.052.

v = (0.0429 × 72.3) / (72.3 + 0.052)
  = 3.10167 / 72.352
  ≈ 0.042869 → 0.0429 to four decimal places.
